ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a set of coordinate axes, with the positive charge Q located at the origin, marked with a plus sign; the observation point (2,0) is located on the positive direction of the x-axis, that is, to the right of Q. Reasoning: Since Q is a positive charge, the direction of the electric field it produces at (2,0) is away from Q, therefore along the +x direction, with magnitude kQ/2^2 = kQ/4. The newly added charge q is also a positive charge, and can be placed at different positions. If q is placed to the left of (2,0), for example between the origin and (2,0), then the electric field produced by q at (2,0) also points in the +x direction, in the same direction as Q's electric field, so the resultant electric field strength increases. If q is placed to the right of (2,0) and sufficiently far away, then the electric field produced by q at (2,0) points in the -x direction, and its magnitude can be made smaller than the original electric field of Q, therefore it will partially cancel Q's electric field, making the resultant electric field strength decrease. Therefore, as the position of q changes, |E| may either increase or decrease.

method.method_draft: Use a vector-component comparison. Read from the image that the observation point P=(2,0) is horizontally to the right of the positive source charge Q at the origin, so the original field is E_Q = kQ/2^2 in the +x direction. From the text, q is a positive charge whose position can vary. Let q be at a general position (a,b). The field contribution of q at P points from q toward P, so its x-component is proportional to 2-a and its y-component is proportional to -b. If a<2, the added field has a positive x-component, and especially when placed on the x-axis to the left of P, it adds directly to E_Q, increasing |E|. If q is placed on the x-axis with a>2, its field is purely in the -x direction; by choosing it far enough to the right, its magnitude is less than E_Q, so the total magnitude becomes E_Q - E_q, which is smaller than E_Q. Therefore varying q's position can make |E| increase or decrease.
